successors.name: Tibetan Empire
successors.text: the Tuyuhun lands around Qinghai Lake, which the Tibetan Empire page says 'was defeated by the Tibetan army and gradually assimilated into Tibetan culture' (663)

rulers.name: Murong Shuluogan
rulers.title: Wuyin Khan / Da Chanyu / Wu King

ledger.x: 284: the Murong Xianbei found the Tuyuhun at Qinghai Lake.
430: the Tuyuhun take what is left of Western Qin.
439: the Tuyuhun spread south into the Qiang country (northern Sichuan side).
469: the Tuyuhun reach west toward the Altun.
476: the Tuyuhun hold the Charklik and Qiemo country.
608: the Sui seize the Tuyuhun lands.
619: Fuyun regains the Tuyuhun lands as the Sui falls.
638: the Tuyuhun lose their south to Tibet.
641: the Tuyuhun lose the Tarim rim.
663: the Tibetan army defeats the Tuyuhun.

wars.name: Tuyuhun conquest of the rest of Western Qin
wars.outcome: The Tuyuhun conquered what was left of Western Qin in 430, leaving Qifu Mumo one city; Xia ended Western Qin at Nan'an in 431, and the Tuyuhun captured Helian Ding of Xia and handed him to Northern Wei in 431.

wars.name: Sui conquest of Tuyuhun
wars.outcome: Tiele attack and Sui occupation in 608 force Fuyun to flee; Fuyun returns in 609 and is driven out again by Emperor Yang in person; the land is held as four commanderies until the Sui collapse.

wars.name: Tang campaign against Tuyuhun
wars.outcome: Li Jing defeats Fuyun in summer 635; Murong Shun is made Prince of Xiping and khan; the Tuyuhun become a Tang vassal without losing land.

wars.name: Tibetan conquest of Tuyuhun
wars.outcome: Songtsen Gampo defeats the Tuyuhun near Qinghai Lake in 634; the Tibetans take southern territory soon after; the kingdom is defeated in 663 (other pages: 669, 670).

wars.name: Battle of Dafeichuan
wars.outcome: Tibetan pyrrhic victory: Xue Rengui's Tang army sent to restore the Tuyuhun retreats; the Tuyuhun are not restored and the Tibetan Empire holds their land.

certainty.note: Highland and steppe frontiers throughout; no page opened gives a treaty or survey line for the Tuyuhun.
